Two things live under **More → Tools** in your workspace: a snippet that
adds a Rumizi button to your own website, and a pair of bookmarklets for
pulling content off pages Rumizi can't crawl on its own.

Direct URL: `rumizi.com/your-venue/w/tools`.

## Add Rumizi to your website

If you already have a website — WordPress, Squarespace, Shopify, or plain
HTML — you can drop in a floating button that opens your Rumizi page in a
new tab. Visitors get to your live menu and the assistant without you
rebuilding anything.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Customise the button">
    Four pickers, with a live preview of a fake website next to them so
    you can see the result before you touch your site:

    - **Theme** — Terracotta, Cream, or Dark.
    - **Shape** — Round, Pill, or Square.
    - **Size** — Small, Medium, or Large.
    - **Position** — Bottom right or Bottom left.

    On the **Pill** shape you can also set the **button label** — it
    defaults to *"Chat with us"*. The round and square shapes are
    icon-only, so the label field is disabled there.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Copy the snippet">
    Copy the `<script>` tag the page generates for you.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Paste it into your site">
    Paste it just before the closing `</body>` tag, on **every page** you
    want the button to appear on. Most site builders have a "custom code"
    or "footer scripts" box for exactly this.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Done">
    Reload your site and the button appears in the corner you picked.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Change your mind about the look later? Re-generate the snippet with new
options and replace the old one. There's nothing stored on Rumizi's side —
the appearance lives entirely in the snippet.
</Tip>

## Browser bookmarklets

Some restaurant websites can't be read automatically — they sit behind
Cloudflare, or build the page with JavaScript after it loads. The
bookmarklets get around this by running in **your** browser, on a page
you're already looking at, so the site sees a normal visitor.

There are two:

<Columns cols={2}>
  <Card title="Capture Menu Content" icon="book-open">
    Grabs the page's text for menu extraction. Use it on a page showing
    food and drink items with prices, then run it through
    [Upload a menu file](/vendors/menu/upload).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Capture Gallery Images" icon="image">
    Finds the photos on a page and imports them into your
    [gallery](/vendors/media/gallery). Use it on pages with food or
    venue photography.
  </Card>
</Columns>

### Using one

<Steps>
  <Step title="Drag it to your bookmarks bar">
    On the Tools page, drag the bookmarklet link up to your browser's
    bookmarks bar. You only do this once.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Go to the page you want">
    Open the restaurant's own website — the menu page, or a page with the
    photos you want.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Click the bookmarklet">
    A small popup confirms what was captured.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Pick it up in Rumizi">
    Captured text shows up in your menu uploads; captured images show up
    in your gallery.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
The bookmarklets use your existing browser session to know who you are, so
**stay signed in to Rumizi** in the same browser. If nothing seems to
happen, that's usually why.
</Note>

<Warning>
Only capture from sites you have the right to use — your own website, or
one you own the photos on. Rumizi doesn't check this for you.
</Warning>
